cues.en: Hi, everyone.
cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: Two
cues.zh: 两

cues.en: years ago,
cues.zh: 年前，

cues.en: my life changed forever.
cues.zh: 我的人生彻底改变了。

cues.en: My wife Kelsey and I
cues.zh: 我和妻子 Kelsey

cues.en: welcomed our daughter Leila into the world.
cues.zh: 迎来了女儿 Leila 的降生。

cues.en: Now, becoming a parent is an amazing,
cues.zh: 当父母是一种奇妙、

cues.en: amazing experience.
cues.zh: 奇妙的体验。

cues.en: Your whole world changes
cues.zh: 你的整个世界会改变

cues.en: overnight,
cues.zh: 一夜之间，

cues.en: and all of your priorities change immediately,
cues.zh: 所有优先级立刻改变，

cues.en: so fast
cues.zh: 快得

cues.en: that it makes it really difficult to process
cues.zh: 让人很难消化

cues.en: sometimes.
cues.zh: 有时。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: you also have to learn a tremendous amount about being a parent, like, for example,
cues.zh: 你还得学大量当父母的知识，比如，

cues.en: how to dress your child.
cues.zh: 怎么给孩子穿衣服。

cues.en: This was new to me. I I I... This is an actual outfit. I thought this was a good idea.
cues.zh: 这对我很新鲜。我我我……这是实际穿的一套。我还以为这主意不错。

cues.en: And even Leila knows that it's not a good idea.
cues.zh: 连 Leila 都知道这主意不怎么样。

cues.en: So there was so much to learn and so much craziness all at once.
cues.zh: 所以一下子有太多要学，也有太多疯狂的事。

cues.en: And to add to the craziness,
cues.zh: 更疯狂的是，

cues.en: Kelsey and I both work from home. We're entrepreneurs. We run our own businesses.
cues.zh: 我和 Kelsey 都在家工作。我们是创业者。我们经营自己的生意。

cues.en: So Kelsey is a...
cues.zh: 所以 Kelsey 是……

cues.en: Develops courses online for yoga teachers.
cues.zh: 她为瑜伽老师开发在线课程。

cues.en: I'm an author. And so I'm working from home. Kelsey's working from home. We have an infant, and we're trying to to make sure that everything gets done that that needs done.
cues.zh: 我是作家。所以我在家工作。Kelsey 也在家工作。我们有个婴儿，还要努力确保该做的事都做完。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: life is really, really,
cues.zh: 生活真的真的、

cues.en: really busy.
cues.zh: 真的非常忙。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: a couple weeks into this amazing experience,
cues.zh: 进入这段奇妙经历几周后，

cues.en: when the sleep deprivation
cues.zh: 当睡眠不足

cues.en: really
cues.zh: 真的

cues.en: kicked in, like around week eight,
cues.zh: 开始发作时，大概第八周，

cues.en: I had this thought,
cues.zh: 我有了一个想法，

cues.en: and it was the same thought that parents
cues.zh: 这也是父母们

cues.en: across
cues.zh: 跨越

cues.en: the ages internationally,
cues.zh: 各个时代、世界各地，

cues.en: everybody has had this thought, which is,
cues.zh: 每个人都有过的想法，就是：

cues.en: I am never going to have free time
cues.zh: 我再也不会有空闲时间

cues.en: ever again.
cues.zh: 了。

cues.en: And this this... Somebody said it's true. Yeah. It's it's not exactly true,
cues.zh: 而这这……有人说这是真的。是啊。也不完全对，

cues.en: but it feels
cues.zh: 但感觉上

cues.en: really,
cues.zh: 真的、

cues.en: really true in that moment. And this this was really disconcerting to me because one of the things that I enjoy
cues.zh: 真的就是那样。而这这让我很不安，因为我最喜欢的事情之一

cues.en: more than anything else is learning new things.
cues.zh: 胜过一切的就是学新东西。

cues.en: Getting curious about something and diving in and fiddling around and learning through trial and error, and eventually becoming pretty good at something.
cues.zh: 对某件事产生好奇，深入进去，瞎折腾，通过试错来学习，最终变得相当擅长。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: without this this free time, I didn't know how I was ever going to do that ever again.
cues.zh: 没有这这空闲时间，我不知道自己还怎么能再做这件事。

cues.en: And so, I'm a big geek.
cues.zh: 所以，我是个超级极客。

cues.en: I want to keep learning things. I want to keep growing.
cues.zh: 我想继续学习东西。我想继续成长。

cues.en: And so, what I decided to do was
cues.zh: 于是我决定做的是

cues.en: go to the library
cues.zh: 去图书馆

cues.en: and go to the bookstore and look at what research says about how we learn and how we learn quickly.
cues.zh: 去书店，看看研究怎么说我们如何学习、如何快速学习。

cues.en: And I read a bunch of books, I read a bunch of websites,
cues.zh: 我读了一堆书，看了一堆网站，

cues.en: and trying to answer this question, how long does it take to acquire a new skill?
cues.zh: 想回答这个问题：掌握一项新技能需要多久？

cues.en: You know what I found?
cues.zh: 你知道我发现了什么吗？

cues.en: Ten thousand
cues.zh: 一万

cues.en: hours.
cues.zh: 小时。

cues.en: Anybody ever heard this? Ten thousand... It takes ten thousand hours. If you want if you want to learn something new, if you want to be good at it, it's gonna take ten thousand hours to get there.
cues.zh: 有人听过这个说法吗？一万……需要一万小时。如果你想如果你想学新东西，如果你想擅长它，那得花一万小时才能达到。

cues.en: And I read this in book after book, and website after website,
cues.zh: 我在一本又一本书、一个又一个网站上读到这个，

cues.en: and the...
My my mental experience of of reading all of this stuff was like, no.
cues.zh: 我我读所有这些内容时的心理感受就是：不。

cues.en: I don't have time. I don't have I don't have ten thousand hours.
cues.zh: 我没时间。我没有，我没有一万小时。

cues.en: I am never going to be able to learn anything new
cues.zh: 我永远都没法学会任何新东西

cues.en: ever again.
cues.zh: 再也不可能了。

cues.en: But that's not true. So ten thousand hours, just to give you a rough order of magnitude, ten thousand hours is a full time job
cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。一万小时，粗略给个数量级，一万小时相当于一份全职工作

cues.en: for five years.
cues.zh: 干五年。

cues.en: That's a long time. We've all had the experience of learning something new, and it didn't take us anywhere close to that amount of time. Right?
cues.zh: 这可太长了。我们都学过新东西，花的时间远没那么多，对吧？

cues.en: So what's up? There's something kind of funky going on here. What the research says and what we expect and have experiences,
cues.zh: 那怎么回事？这里有点蹊跷。研究结论，与我们的预期和实际经历，

cues.en: they don't match up.
cues.zh: 对不上。

cues.en: And what I found...
cues.zh: 而我发现……

cues.en: Here's the wrinkle.
cues.zh: 问题就在这儿。

cues.en: The ten thousand hour rule came out of studies of expert
cues.zh: 一万小时定律源自对专家

cues.en: level performance.
cues.zh: 级表现的研究。

cues.en: There was a professor at Florida State University. His name is Kay Anders Ericsson. He's the originator of the ten thousand hour rule.
cues.zh: 佛罗里达州立大学有位教授，名叫 Kay Anders Ericsson。他是一万小时定律的提出者。

cues.en: And where that came from is he studied
cues.zh: 这个结论来自他研究

cues.en: professional athletes,
cues.zh: 职业运动员、

cues.en: world class musicians,
cues.zh: 世界级音乐家、

cues.en: chess grandmasters,
cues.zh: 国际象棋特级大师、

cues.en: all of these ultra competitive folks in ultra high performing fields,
cues.zh: 所有这些身处超高绩效领域的顶尖竞争者，

cues.en: and he tried to figure out how long does it take to get to the top
cues.zh: 他想弄清，要花多久才能登上

cues.en: of those kinds of fields. And what he found is the more deliberate practice, the more time that those individuals spent practicing the elements, whatever it is that they do, the more time you spend, the better you get. And the folks at the tippy top of their fields
cues.zh: 这类领域的顶峰。他发现，刻意练习越多，这些人在自己所做的各个要素上练习的时间越多，你花的时间越多，就变得越好。而那些领域最顶尖的人

cues.en: put in around ten thousand hours of practice.
cues.zh: 投入了大约一万小时练习。

cues.en: Now, we're talking about the game of telephone a little bit earlier.
cues.zh: 我们前面聊到过传话游戏。

cues.en: Here's what happened.
cues.zh: 事情是这样的。

cues.en: An author by the name of Malcolm Gladwell
cues.zh: 一位名叫 Malcolm Gladwell 的作者

cues.en: wrote a book, in 2007 called Outliers, The Story of Success. And the centerpiece of that book was the ten thousand hour rule. Practice a lot, practice well,
cues.zh: 在 2007 年写了本书，叫 Outliers: The Story of Success。书的核心就是一万小时定律。大量练习、练得好，

cues.en: and you will do extremely
cues.zh: 你就会极其

cues.en: well. You reach the top of your field.
cues.zh: 出色。你会达到所在领域的顶峰。

cues.en: So the message, what doctor Anders... Erickson was actually saying is,
cues.zh: 所以，Anders... Ericsson 博士真正想说的是，

cues.en: it takes ten thousand hours to get to the top of an ultra competitive field in a very narrow subject.
cues.zh: 要在一个非常狭窄的科目里，达到极度竞争领域的顶峰，需要一万小时。

cues.en: That's what that means.
cues.zh: 这就是它的意思。

cues.en: But here's what happened. Ever since Outliers came out,
cues.zh: 但后来发生了什么呢？自从 Outliers 出版，

cues.en: immediately came out, reached the top of the best seller list, stayed there for three solid months,
cues.zh: 一出版就登上畅销榜榜首，稳稳待了整整三个月，

cues.en: all of a sudden, the ten thousand hour rule was everywhere.
cues.zh: 突然间，一万小时定律无处不在。

cues.en: And a society wide game of telephone
cues.zh: 一场全社会范围的传话游戏

cues.en: started to be played.
cues.zh: 开始上演。

cues.en: So this message, it takes ten thousand hours to reach the top of an ultra competitive field,
cues.zh: 于是，这个信息——要花一万小时才能达到超竞争领域的顶峰——

cues.en: became,
cues.zh: 变成了，

cues.en: it takes ten thousand hours to become an expert
cues.zh: 要花一万小时才能成为专家

cues.en: at something,
cues.zh: 在某件事上，

cues.en: which became it takes ten thousand hours to become
cues.zh: 又变成了，要花一万小时才能变得

cues.en: good at something, which became
cues.zh: 擅长某件事，再变成了

cues.en: it takes ten thousand hours to learn
cues.zh: 要花一万小时才能学会

cues.en: something.
cues.zh: 某件事。

cues.en: But that last statement, it takes ten thousand hours to learn something, it's not true.
cues.zh: 但最后这句话——要学会某件事需要一万小时——并不正确。

cues.en: It's not true.
cues.zh: 这并不是真的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: what the research actually says, if if... I I spent a lot of time here at the CSU library in the cognitive psychology stacks because I'm a geek.
cues.zh: 研究到底表明了什么？因为我是个极客，我在 CSU 图书馆的认知心理学书库里泡了很久。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: when you actually look at the studies of skill acquisition,
cues.zh: 当你真正去查阅技能习得相关的研究时，

cues.en: you see over and over and over a graph like this.
cues.zh: 你会反复看到这样一张图表。

cues.en: Now, researchers,
cues.zh: 研究人员呢，

cues.en: whether they're studying a motor skill,
cues.zh: 无论他们研究的是运动技能，

cues.en: something you do physically, or a mental skill,
cues.zh: 也就是身体动作，还是心智技能，

cues.en: they like to study things that they can time
cues.zh: 他们都喜欢研究能掐表计时的东西，

cues.en: because you can quantify that. Right? So they'll give research participants a little task, something that requires physical arrangement or something that requires learn... Learning a little
cues.zh: 因为这样能量化，对吧？所以他们会给被试一个简单任务，比如某种肢体操作，或者学会某种

cues.en: mental trick, and they'll time how long a participant takes
cues.zh: 思维技巧，然后记录被试需要多长时间

cues.en: to complete the skill.
cues.zh: 才能完成这项技能。

cues.en: And here's what this graph says. When you start, so when researchers gave participants a task, it took them a really long time because it was new and they were horrible.
cues.zh: 这张图表达的就是这个意思。刚开始时，研究人员布置了任务，被试要花很长时间，因为是全新的任务，而且他们做得很差。

cues.en: With a little bit of practice,
cues.zh: 经过一点点练习，

cues.en: they get better and better and better, and the early part of practice is really really efficient. People get good at things
cues.zh: 他们就越来越熟练，初期的练习效率非常非常高。人们擅长做某件事，

cues.en: with just a little bit of practice.
cues.zh: 往往只需要一点点练习。

cues.en: Now, what's interesting to note is that
cues.zh: 不过，值得注意且有趣的是，

cues.en: if, you know, we don't really...
cues.zh: 如果我们……你知道，我们其实并不……

cues.en: For skills that we want to learn for ourselves, we don't care so much about time. Right? We just care about how good we are, whatever good happens to me.
cues.zh: 对于自己想学的技能，我们其实不太在意时间，对吧？我们只在乎自己水平有多好，不管这个“好”对自己意味着什么。

cues.en: So if we relabel performance time to how good you are,
cues.zh: 所以，如果我们把“耗费时间”替换为“水平高低”，

cues.en: the graph flips.
cues.zh: 图表就反过来了。

cues.en: And you get this famous and widely known, this is the learning curve.
cues.zh: 这就得到了大名鼎鼎、人尽皆知的——学习曲线。

cues.en: And the story of the learning curve is when you start, you're grossly incompetent and you know it. Right?
cues.zh: 学习曲线想表达的是：刚开始时，你极其笨拙，而且你自己也心知肚明，对吧？

cues.en: With a little bit of practice, you get really good really quick. So that early level of improvement is really fast.
cues.zh: 只要稍加练习，你就会飞速进步。前期的提升非常快。

cues.en: And then at a certain point, you reach a plateau
cues.zh: 但到了某个节点，你会进入平台期，

cues.en: and the subsequent gains become
cues.zh: 随后的提升就会

cues.en: much harder to get. They take more time to to to get. Now,
cues.zh: 变得艰难得多。需要花多得多的时间才能取得进步。那么，

cues.en: my question is,
cues.zh: 我的问题是，

cues.en: I want that.
cues.zh: 我想要达到那个状态。

cues.en: Right? How long does it take from starting something and being grossly incompetent in knowing it
cues.zh: 对吧？从零开始、笨手笨脚且自知很菜，

cues.en: to being reasonably good
cues.zh: 到达到“相当不错”的水平，

cues.en: in, hopefully, as short a period of time as possible?
cues.zh: 在尽可能短的时间内，到底需要多久？

cues.en: So how long does that take? Here's what my research says.
cues.zh: 那到底要多久？我的调研结果是：

cues.en: Twenty hours.
cues.zh: 20 个小时。

cues.en: That's it.
cues.zh: 仅此而已。

cues.en: You can go from knowing nothing
cues.zh: 你可以从一无所知，

cues.en: about any skill that you can think of. Wanna learn a language?
cues.zh: 到掌握任何你能想到的技能。想学一门外语？

cues.en: Wanna learn how to draw?
cues.zh: 想学画画？

cues.en: Want to learn how to juggle flaming chainsaws?
cues.zh: 想学抛接带火的电锯杂耍？

cues.en: If you put twenty hours of focused,
cues.zh: 只要你投入 20 个小时进行专注、

cues.en: deliberate practice into that thing, you will be astounded,
cues.zh: 刻意的练习，你就会感到震惊，

cues.en: astounded
cues.zh: 彻底震惊于

cues.en: at how good you are.
cues.zh: 自己居然能变得这么厉害。

cues.en: Twenty hours is doable. That's about forty five minutes a day for about a month,
cues.zh: 20 个小时是完全可行的。大约是一个月内每天练 45 分钟，

cues.en: even skipping a couple days here and there. Twenty hours isn't that hard to accumulate.
cues.zh: 偶尔中间漏掉几天也没关系。凑够 20 个小时并不难。

cues.en: Now, there's a method to doing this because it's not like you can just start fiddling around for about twenty hours and expect these massive improvements.
cues.zh: 不过，这套方法是有讲究的，因为你不可能随便瞎捣鼓 20 个小时，就指望能有突飞猛进的提升。

cues.en: There's a way to practice intelligently.
cues.zh: 有一种聪明的练习方法。

cues.en: There's a way to practice efficiently
cues.zh: 有一种高效的练习方法，

cues.en: that will make sure that you invest those twenty hours
cues.zh: 能确保你投入的这 20 个小时

cues.en: in the most effective way that you possibly can. And here's the method. It applies to anything.
cues.zh: 产生尽可能最大的效果。方法就在这里，它适用于任何技能。

cues.en: The first
cues.zh: 第一点，

cues.en: is to deconstruct the skill. Decide exactly
cues.zh: 解构技能。明确决定

cues.en: what you want to be able to do when you're done,
cues.zh: 你学完之后究竟想做到什么，

cues.en: and then look into the skill and break it down
cues.zh: 然后审视这项技能，把它拆解

cues.en: into smaller and smaller pieces.
cues.zh: 成越来越小的组成部分。

cues.en: Most of the things that we think of as skills
cues.zh: 我们通常认为的“一项技能”，

cues.en: are actually big bundles of skills that that require all sorts of different things. The more you can break apart the skill,
cues.zh: 其实是一整捆技能的集合，涵盖了各种不同的能力。你把技能拆得越细，

cues.en: the more you're able to decide what are the parts of this skill that will actually help me get to what I want,
cues.zh: 就越能弄清哪些部分才能真正帮你达到目标，

cues.en: and then you can practice those first.
cues.zh: 接着你就可以先去练这些部分。

cues.en: And if you practice the most important things first, you'll be able to improve your performance
cues.zh: 如果你先练习最重要的部分，就能在最短的时间内

cues.en: in the least amount of time possible.
cues.zh: 尽可能提升自己的水平。

cues.en: The second is learn enough to self correct.
cues.zh: 第二点，学到足以自我纠错就够了。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 也就是说，

cues.en: get three to five resources about what it is you're trying to learn. It could be books, could be DVDs,
cues.zh: 找三到五份你想学的相关资料。可以是书，可以是视频光盘，

cues.en: could be courses, could be anything.
cues.zh: 可以是课程，什么都行。

cues.en: But don't use those as a as a way to procrastinate
cues.zh: 但别把它们当成拖延练习

cues.en: on practice. I I I know I do this. Right? Get like 20 books about the topic. It's like, I'm gonna start learning how to program
cues.zh: 的借口。我知道我自己就会这样，对吧？比如买上 20 本相关主题的书，想着“等我读完这 20 本书，

cues.en: a computer when I complete these 20 books. No. That's procrastination.
cues.zh: 我就开始学编程”。别这样，这就是拖延。

cues.en: What you want to do is learn just enough
cues.zh: 你要做的是学到刚刚好，

cues.en: that you can actually practice and self correct
cues.zh: 刚好能让你真正开始练习，

cues.en: or self edit
cues.zh: 并在练习过程中

cues.en: as you practice.
cues.zh: 自我纠错或调整。

cues.en: So the learning becomes a way of getting better
cues.zh: 这样学习就变成了一种途径，让你更容易

cues.en: at noticing when you're making a mistake
cues.zh: 察觉到自己什么时候犯了错，

cues.en: and then doing something a little different.
cues.zh: 然后做些微调。

cues.en: The third
cues.zh: 第三点，

cues.en: is to remove barriers to practice.
